GS reports its provision for credit losses increased to $1.54 billion from $1.14 billion, primarily driven by net charge-offs in its credit card portfolio. Both companies attribute the rise in credit costs to specific loan portfolio performance indicators (spread products for C, credit cards for GS).

comparisons.peer_topic: Global Private Bank Expense and Credit Provision
comparisons.peer_summary: Noninterest expense was $14.4 billion, up 13%, predominantly driven by higher compensation (including revenue-related compensation and growth in private banking advisor teams) and higher distribution fees and legal expense; the provision for credit losses was a net benefit of $68 million compared to a $159 million provision in the prior year, which included a $146 million addition to the allowance for First Republic loans.
comparisons.comparison: Both C and JPM disclose specific credit provision activity in 2024, though with opposite financial impacts. C reports an increase in cost of credit ($463 million). In contrast, JPM's Global Private Bank reports a net benefit (negative provision) of $68 million for credit losses, a significant improvement from the prior year's $159 million provision. Both disclosures isolate credit performance to specific business units or segments (C's Markets segment and JPM's Global Private Bank), allowing for a direct comparison of credit loss experience within those units.
